title: City-States and Democracy
text:
Ancient Greece on a timeline




776 BC · The first recorded Olympic GamesOlympic Games🔊 奥林匹克运动会🔊Sports contests at Olympia every four years, to honor Zeus.History Vocab ↗ at Olympia.
About 508 BC · Athens starts a democracydemocracy🔊 民主🔊Government where citizens make decisions by voting.History Vocab ↗.
447–432 BC · The Parthenon templetemple🔊 神庙🔊A building where people worship a god or goddess.History Vocab ↗ is built in Athens.
399 BC · The philosopherphilosopher🔊 哲学家🔊A thinker who asks big questions about life and truth.History Vocab ↗ Socrates dies in Athens.




The Parthenon in Athens today, about 2,450 years old.


BC means “before Christ”: the years count down toward year 1. So 776 BC came before 508 BC.

title: City-States and Democracy
text:
Mountains and sea



Greece is a rocky peninsulapeninsula🔊 半岛🔊Land with water on three sides.History Vocab ↗ with many islands.
Mountains split the land into small valleys.
Each valley grew its own city-statecity-state🔊 城邦🔊A city and the land around it, with its own government.History Vocab ↗: one city and its farms.
The sea connected them. Greeks traded by ship and started a colonycolony🔊 殖民地🔊A new town started by people from another city.History Vocab ↗ wherever they found good land.





peninsula 半岛
Land with water on three sides.


colony 殖民地
A new town started by people from another city.

title: City-States and Democracy
text:
Key words: who decides?



city-state 城邦
A city and the land around it, with its own government.


citizen 公民
A member of a city-state with rights, like the right to vote.


democracy 民主
Government where citizens make decisions by voting.


assembly 公民大会
A meeting where citizens discuss and vote on laws.

title: City-States and Democracy
text:
How democracy worked in Athens

The assemblyassembly🔊 公民大会🔊A meeting where citizens discuss and vote on laws.History Vocab ↗ met about 40 times a year on a hill called the Pnyx.
Any citizencitizen🔊 公民🔊A member of a city-state with rights, like the right to vote.History Vocab ↗ could stand up and speak.
Then they voted, usually by raising their hands: votevote🔊 投票🔊To choose officially, for example by raising your hand.History Vocab ↗.
In court, juries of hundreds of citizens voted with small tokens.


Demos = people, kratos = power. Democracy = power of the people.
